images.title: Reading a number with zeros
images.purpose: Show the chart of 30,402 with its two zeros marked as places that are not said, and the number name.
images.composition: The number on top, a one-row chart below it with the zeros highlighted and tagged, and the name on the last line.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. Top: the number 30,402 in very large bold dark numerals (120 px), centred, with the comma clear. Middle: a chart of 5 columns about 220 px wide and 2 rows. Header row: TTh, Th, H, T, O in white bold letters on blue #0072B2 cells. Digit row: 3, 0, 4, 0, 2 in large bold dark numerals (90 px). The two 0 cells (under Th and under T) have a reddish purple #CC79A7 fill; the cells holding 3, 4 and 2 are white. Under each of the two 0 cells a small tag reading not said (36 px, dark) with a short tick pointing up to its cell. Bottom: one line in dark sans-serif (56 px): Thirty thousand four hundred two.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: A zero holds a place in the number but we do not say it when we read the number.
images.description: The number 30,402 above a place value chart with digits 3, 0, 4, 0, 2 where the two zeros are highlighted and tagged not said, and the name Thirty thousand four hundred two below.
images.context: Concept image for Reading numbers with zeros. The figure in your maths book shows the zero places of numbers such as 10,010 and 50,005; this image uses the video's own example, 30,402.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the students to read the number first and see whether they say zero. Stress that the zeros must stay in the number, because they keep the other digits in their places. Only the reading skips them.

image_decisions.why: A highlighted chart of 30,402 shows which places hold a zero and are skipped when we read.
